_notes: symbol_map remaps an OLD ticker onto its SUCCESSOR ticker before the FIFO
engine runs. Once remapped, the '-X of old / +Y of new' pair becomes a
same-symbol share-count change, which the engine treats as basis-preserving.
A CUSIP appears here when Schwab books a merger by REMOVING the position
under its ticker and RE-ADDING it under a CUSIP. The subsequent sale is then
recorded against the CUSIP, so without the mapping the old ticker keeps a
phantom position holding the real cost, while the CUSIP realizes the whole
proceeds against zero basis. Wrong in both directions at once.
Seeded from mergers/renames actually present in the Schwab history.
Anything the engine cannot explain lands in anomalies.csv -- add it here.
